amendments.reason: m2-fix-doctrine.c2's authored check used 'grep -L PATTERN file && ...': grep -L exits 1 exactly when it successfully finds/prints a file with no match (POSIX/GNU semantics -- exit status tracks match/no-match, not what -L inverts for display), so the && chain can never reach the second grep once 'must be told' is genuinely removed -- a check that cannot pass. Verified live: 'grep -L "must be told" commander-core.md' prints the filename (correct: no match) but exits 1. Corrected to '! grep -q PATTERN file && grep -l ...', which asserts the same two facts (absence + presence) without the -L exit-status trap. Verified the corrected command exits 0 against the already-edited files.
